Geoff Goode won the 1 mile, with Brian Trower second, and the latter looks like following in his brother's footsteps as a future club champion.

Geoff Goode and Brian Trower were first two home in the mile and Trower also won the Javelin event, much to his surprise ! Jim Purdy won the High Jump and also gained third place in the Javelin, while Frank Kemp won the Shott Putt and it was a case of everyone having a go at everything !

Brian Trower won an exciting junior mile and our juniors also won their medley relay. After the running, the teams adjourned to the Village Hall for " light " refreshment and it was quite an eye-opener to see how our juniors " knocked " it back !

Brian Trower was third and here again the time was very good for juniors. The one mile senior was the race of the afternoon, with a very strong field turning out, but Jack Brown, the holder, ran a well-judged race to come away over the last 200 yards to beat Len Herbert and Chas.

In the Junior events we saw Alan Law score a good double by winning the 100 and 220 yards, while Brian Trower was another dual winner in the 440 and 880 with Boreham giving him good assistance in both races.

Brian Trower writes us from the Fighter Plotters School at Middle Wallop, while J. Hills is with the R.A.S.C. at Aldershot, and Don Maclean is now with the R.A. in North Wales and says he is hoping to get in some running while there.

Brian Trower finished third in the Portsmouth A.C. open 5 miles road handicap race, with a start of 3 min. 10 secs., and has also been running with the R.A.F., Sopley.
We had to go back to 125th position for our next scorer, B. Trower, who was ten places in front of Frank Wright whose running seems to have been upset by an Army P.T.I.
One of our juniors, Brian Trower, had hung on to the back of the bunch and ran well on the way back to finish 8th. Herbert was the winner in 23.56, with Smart 24.5 and Short 24.17.
In the first few hundred yards Brian Trower again tried to show us all the way but Bill Pawsey soon took over the lead which he held to the end.
Brian Trower, "A", ran a well judged race to finish 25th, one place ahead of Paterson. Eric Gebbett and Colin Collis both ran very soundly to finish 47th and 58th respectively.

There was a considerable amount of speculation before the race as to the merits of Brian Trower and of course, D. Chevalier, who has been showing rapid improvement, could not be left out of the reckoning.
With our team at full strength, we must have secured a place. B. Trower was our first runner home in 10th position (29.08), G.
